By definition, any real number $y \ge 1$ serves as an upper bound for this interval. For example, if we let $y = 1$, then for every $x \in [0, 1]$, the condition $x \le 1$ (and thus $y \ge x$) is satisfied by the definition of the closed interval $[0, 1]$. Since such a real number $y$ exists, the statement is true.
